author: massicomar
title: Subtree
summary:
There is a tree with $N$ vertices, numbered $1, 2, \ldots, N$. For each $i$ ($1 \leq i \leq N - 1$), the $i$-th edge connects Vertex $x_i$ and $y_i$.

Taro has decided to paint each vertex in white or black, so that any black vertex can be reached from any other black vertex by passing through only black vertices.

You are given a positive integer $M$. For each $v$ ($1 \leq v \leq N$), answer the following question:

- Assuming that Vertex $v$ has to be black, find the number of ways in which the vertices can be painted, modulo $M$.

Input

Input is given from Standard Input in the following format:

$N$ $M$
$x_1$ $y_1$
$x_2$ $y_2$
$:$
$x_{N - 1}$ $y_{N - 1}$

Output

Print $N$ lines. The $v$-th ($1 \leq v \leq N$) line should contain the answer to the following question:

- Assuming that Vertex $v$ has to be black, find the number of ways in which the vertices can be painted, modulo $M$.

constraints.text: N ≤ 1e5, answers modulo any M ≤ 1e9 (not necessarily prime)

explanation: For every vertex v, count connected black sets containing v. Rerooting: a downward pass for subtrees, an upward pass for 'everything outside', using prefix/suffix products because M may not be prime.
traps: You can't divide by (down[c] + 1) to exclude a child: M isn't prime and the value may be 0 mod M.

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: down[v] = # connected black sets inside v's subtree that contain v; up[v] = the same for the part outside v's subtree, hanging from v's parent
dp[v] = # connected black sets in v's subtree containing v, recomputed with every vertex as root
options.why: Right DP, but N roots × O(N) = 1e10.

options.text: dp[mask] = whether black set mask is connected
dp[v][c] = colourings of v's subtree with v coloured c
options.why: That's Independent Set's state; this problem needs connectivity to v.

extraLayers.explanation: 'Answer for every root' is the rerooting signal: one DP for inside the subtree, one for outside.

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.text: down[v] = Π (down[c] + 1); ans[v] = down[v] · (up[v] + 1); up[c] = (up[v] + 1) · Π over siblings s ≠ c of (down[s] + 1) via prefix/suffix products

options.why: Division is unsafe: M isn't prime.
Choices in different child subtrees multiply.
Same answer for every vertex — ignores the 'must contain v' part.

extraLayers.explanation: Each child is either cut off (1) or connected (down[c] ways); the outside part works the same way through the parent.

es.explanation: Para cada vértice v, cuenta los conjuntos negros conexos que contienen a v. Rerooting: una pasada hacia abajo para los subárboles y otra hacia arriba para “todo lo de afuera”, con productos de prefijos y sufijos porque M puede no ser primo.
traps: No puedes dividir por (down[c] + 1) para excluir a un hijo: M no es primo y el valor puede ser 0 mod M.

dp-state.explanation: “La respuesta para cada raíz” es la señal de rerooting: una DP para adentro del subárbol y otra para afuera.

why.b: La DP es la correcta, pero N raíces × O(N) = 1e10.
why.d: Ese es el estado de Independent Set; este problema necesita conexión con v.

dp-transition.explanation: Cada hijo queda cortado (1) o conectado (down[c] formas); la parte de afuera funciona igual, a través del padre.

why.b: Dividir no es seguro: M no es primo.
why.c: Las elecciones en subárboles de hijos distintos se multiplican.
why.d: Da la misma respuesta para todos los vértices: ignora que tiene que contener a v.
